claims.text: The Glean Agent Building Competency certifies partner teams to design, build, govern, and operationalize production-grade Glean Agents that automate workflows and deliver measurable business outcomes.
The Agent Building Competency focuses on persona-aligned agent design, prompt engineering, tool use, governance, and operational best practices across the agent lifecycle.
One competency requirement is completing 5 technical accreditations within the Glean Partner Portal, validated by a Glean Partner Manager.
One competency requirement is completing a Glean-delivered agent building workshop session with your Glean technical team, validated by a Glean Partner Solutions Engineer.
The competency requires building 5 functioning, production-ready agents.
Each of the 5 competency agents must implement at least 3 discrete steps beyond simple retrieval, including at least one thinking or transformation step.
Each of the 5 competency agents must configure retrieval guardrails so the agent uses a well-defined set of content sources and has clear instructions for what it can and cannot answer.
Each of the 5 competency agents must contain explicit error-handling with a defined fallback behavior for low-confidence or out-of-scope questions.
At least 1 of the 5 competency agents must invoke actions or tools that write to other systems.
At least 1 of the 5 competency agents must call more than one tool or system in a single run.
At least 1 of the 5 competency agents must use conditional branching.
At least 1 of the 5 competency agents must use loops to process a collection.
At least 1 of the 5 competency agents must use a schedule-based trigger.
At least 1 of the 5 competency agents must use an event or content-based trigger.
For each competency agent, partners must gather business and technical requirements with the end user, evidenced by a document outlining those requirements.

Competency validation includes a call with a Glean Partner Solutions Engineer to review the finalized agents; partners should expect to walk through and run each agent on the call, and ideally provide a recorded walkthrough beforehand.
For each competency agent, partners must complete an agent architecture review with a Glean technical resource, outlining best practices followed and agent structure.
For each competency agent, partners must provide a written outline of the agent's business impact and why a Glean Agent was the best solution, reviewed by a Glean Partner Solutions Engineer.

Competency benefits include market visibility as a trusted Glean Partner, a Glean Partner Competency Badge, access to Glean services opportunities, being surfaced to Glean sellers as a preferred services partner, and a searchable directory listing.
Agent Building Competency benefits include priority consideration for agent-focused services opportunities and co-marketing opportunities that highlight agent outcomes and ROI.
The Competency Program is open to all registered Glean Partners, including resell, services, and ISV or product partners, and the organization must already be a registered Glean Partner.
Glean competencies require thorough experience and successful completion of an audit process.
The Agent Building Competency Submission Workbook is available in the Glean Partner Portal Asset Library.
ACC-104 is the badge for builders who can implement actions, agents, and connectors, assessed by a capstone lab.
